"Pre-main amplifier using H-R IC pulse power supply.H-R IC pulse power supply is used for the power supply.This power supply directly rectifies the AC power source to direct current, then converts it into ultra-high frequency pulses of 35kHz, and step-down and rectifies it with a high-frequency ferrite core transformer to obtain the desired DC voltage.In addition, feedback is applied from the DC output terminal of the power supply. The voltage fluctuation at the output terminal is detected by an error amplifier circuit, and the signal is transmitted to a pulse width modulator by a photocoupler. In the pulse width modulator, a constant voltage is controlled by a PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) control method that controls the total time of switching transistors. In the PWM control, the pulse width is narrowed when the DC output voltage rises above 40v, and is widened when the DC output voltage falls.In the pulse power supply, the voltage fluctuation detection part is rectified by direct current (DC) and passed through the smoothing circuit. Then, it is located at the output terminal of the power supply Kario. All of the power supply circuit is included in the feedback loop for stabilization, so that the voltage fluctuation is very small. This was achieved by the development of a hybrid IC capable of high-voltage switching and high-speed switching. The number of parts has been reduced significantly and reliability has been improved.Since the pulse power supply deals with high frequencies, if it leaks outside, it will have a large effect on the amplifier. To prevent this, the whole unit is CAN shielded to reduce unnecessary radiation.The power amplifier circuit consists of FET source follower differential input, second stage emitter follower differential amplification, and low distortion power IC.The power ICs are Darlington 2-stage pure complimentary service and DC-amplifier configuration, and the transistors used in each stage are specially selected low-noise high-ft transistors.The tone control circuit uses BAX type.The circuit is composed of an emitter-follower input and a tone control IC. name: DCC-3001
description:
## Description

"A control amplifier developed with the theme of absolute precision, aiming to be one of the amplifiers that continue to live in history.The DCC-3001is designed to improve TID (transient intermodulation distortion) by using a large amount of negative feedback. Measures such as applying local negative feedback at each stage until the final stage are taken to improve bare characteristics, and these are connected in cascade to obtain the best overall characteristics with the minimum overall negative feedback. This eliminates the delay phase correction capacitor for oscillation prevention, which is indispensable when deep overall negative feedback is used, and achieves excellent slew rate.In addition, the dynamic range in the first stage is expanded by inserting a high resistance as a local negative feedback into both emitters of the first stage differential amplifier. At the same time, the naked characteristics are improved by the effect of the advanced phase correction circuit inserted in this stage, and it can be used without feedback.The equalizer circuit is a fully developed power amplifier circuit.All stages are directly connected, consisting of two stages of differential amplifier and a current mirror type phase-inverted class A push-pull output stage. To prevent bias fluctuation due to power supply voltage fluctuation, both the first stage and the second stage differential amplifier are provided with a constant current circuit using transistors. The fluctuation of midpoint potential is strictly controlled by a perfectly symmetric current mirror circuit. The capacitor for 100% DC feedback, which is inserted in series with a resistor in the base of the first stage differential amplifier, is removed, and the same negative feedback from AC to DC is used to improve the transient response in the low range.This circuit achieves a gain of 40dB and a large allowable input of 500mV. This large allowable input is achieved by applying a supply voltage as high as ¥75V using transistors of the highest withstand voltage class available. In addition, the second stage differential amplifier has a PNP configuration with the same polarity as the first stage differential amplifier, so that the voltage distribution between them can be freely determined. In addition, the gain is reduced by applying a considerable local negative feedback at the first stage.In addition, the noise level is 1.5Ï‰ V or less, which is the physical noise level of the transistor itself in terms of input conversion. Further improvement can be achieved only by the improvement of the transistor. All the transistors used are of the cancel-type to avoid noise increase due to aging.The RIAA deviation is suppressed to less than ¥0.1dB at 30Hz to 15kHz using a D-rank (more than 0.5% accuracy) NiCr deposition resistor and a Styrofoam capacitor.It has a unique configuration as a control amplifier with a built-in power amplifier for 1W monitor, and can be used as a stand-alone unit.This monitor amplifier is fully Class-A operation. It is complimentary service SEPP system with first stage differential amplifier, two stage common-emitter driver and Darlington emitter-follower. The power supply voltage is ¥35v to the driver stage and ¥6v to the output stage in a vacuum tube fashion.
